name: hubvibe-site-audit
description: HubVibe: 38 Machine-Payable Dev Utilities and WCAG Audits. This MCP server exposes the five deterministic site audits (accessibility via axe-core, SEO, security headers, performance, and the bundle) and the deterministic predictive probability engine (linear regression, normal distribution modeling and p-value validation over inline points or a BigQuery table) as tools. The 38 /work utilities -- LLM inference, web search and extraction, Base chain reads, market and prediction-market data, BigQuery analysis and forecasting, regression and probability statistics, image/speech/video generation, sandboxed Python, maps, cited research and verification -- are plain HTTP routes, priced per call and documented with request and response schemas in /openapi.json, /.well-known/agent.json and /.well-known/ard.json.
note: There IS a live MCP server here: POST to the `remotes[0].url` above (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0; initialize / ping / tools/list / tools/call). `initialize` and `tools/list` are free and unauthenticated, so a client can read this whole catalog and its prices before deciding to spend anything; `tools/call` is billed per call and answers an unpaid call with the payment challenge rather than an error. Each tool's `httpEndpoint` (a non-standard extension field) additionally maps that same tool onto a plain REST route, for callers that would rather POST JSON than speak MCP -- it is an alternative transport to the same audit, not a sign that MCP is unavailable. Both transports are served by one process against one catalog, so their prices and schemas cannot disagree.

auth.note: Populated at serve time from this deployment's live configuration. GET /mcp.json for the authoritative list -- it contains only rails that can genuinely settle here. This file cannot know that, so it does not guess. See also /.well-known/agent.json.

tools.name: hubvibe_predictive_probability_engine
tools.title: Predictive probability engine: regression, normal model, p-values
tools.description: Deterministic statistics over (x, y) points: ordinary least squares linear regression with standard errors and confidence intervals, a fitted normal distribution with quantiles and probability queries, exact Student t and Jarque-Bera p-values validated at your alpha, and predictions with prediction intervals. Points come inline or from a BigQuery table (two numeric columns; above max_rows the rows are chosen by fingerprint, never at random). Pure arithmetic with exactly rounded sums: the same input always returns the same numbers, and no LLM is anywhere in the path. $0.50 per call. Returns: source{}, n, alpha, confidence_level, metrics[], linear_regression{}, normal_distribution{}, p_values{}, prediction[], notes[], method.

points.description: The data: [x, y] pairs (or {x, y} objects), 2 to 100000 of them; at least 3 for a regression. Use this OR `table`.

table.description: BigQuery table to read instead of `points`: project.dataset.table, readable by the node's service account (public datasets are). Needs x_column and y_column.

max_rows.description: Rows to read from `table`, default 10000. A larger table is reduced to this many rows by FARM_FINGERPRINT order, so the same table always yields the same rows.

metrics.description: Which results to compute. Default: linear_regression, normal_distribution and p_values, plus prediction when predict_x is given.

predict_x.description: x values to predict y at, with mean and prediction intervals.

alpha.description: Significance level for p-value validation and intervals. Default 0.05.

distribution_of.description: Which values the normal model fits. Default y.

probability_queries.description: Probabilities to read off the fitted normal model: {"below": v}, {"above": v} or {"between": [a, b]}.

outputSchema.description: The 200 body of every paid /work call. `result` is the worker's own output (its schema is per route); everything else is the same on all 38 routes. A receipt for the job is at `receipt_url`.

status.description: Present only on a delivered result.

worker.description: Catalog name of the worker that ran.

price_usd.description: What this call cost, in USD.

table.description: BigQuery table read, when source is bigquery.

x_column.description: Column used for x, when source is bigquery.

y_column.description: Column used for y, when source is bigquery.

sql.description: The read-only SQL that ran, when source is bigquery.

rows_available.description: Rows with finite x and y in the table; null for inline points.

rows_used.description: Points the statistics were computed from.

sampled.description: True when the table had more usable rows than were read.

gib_processed.description: Gibibytes BigQuery scanned; null for inline points.

source.description: Where the data came from and how much of it was used.

confidence_level.description: 1 - alpha: the level of every interval.

r.description: Pearson correlation; null when y is constant.

r_squared.description: Coefficient of determination; null when y is constant.

adjusted_r_squared.description: R^2 adjusted for degrees of freedom.

residual_std_error.description: Standard error of the residuals, sqrt(SSE / df).

slope_t.description: t statistic of the slope; null when undefined.

intercept_t.description: t statistic of the intercept; null when undefined.

t_critical.description: Two-sided t critical value at alpha with df degrees of freedom.

slope_ci.description: Lower and upper bound at the confidence level.

intercept_ci.description: Lower and upper bound at the confidence level.

f_statistic.description: F statistic of the regression (t^2); null when undefined.

sst.description: Total sum of squares of y.

linear_regression.description: Ordinary least squares fit of y on x; null when not requested.

skewness.description: Sample skewness; null when the values are constant.

excess_kurtosis.description: Excess kurtosis; null when the values are constant.

quantiles.description: Quantiles of the fitted normal; null when degenerate.

normality.description: Jarque-Bera normality test; null when the values are constant.

reject_at_alpha.description: p_value < alpha: not normal at this alpha.

normal_distribution.description: Normal model of the chosen values; null when not requested.

t.description: Student t statistic; null when undefined (a perfect fit).
Student t statistic; null when undefined (a perfect fit).

normality_of_residuals.description: Jarque-Bera normality test; null when the values are constant.

reject_at_alpha.description: p_value < alpha: not normal at this alpha.

p_values.description: Hypothesis tests validated at alpha; null when not requested.

prediction.description: One entry per predict_x; null when not requested.

mean_ci.description: Lower and upper bound at the confidence level.

prediction_interval.description: Lower and upper bound at the confidence level.

items.description: A caveat about a degenerate input.
examples: The points lie exactly on a line.

notes.description: Caveats about the input; empty when there are none.

examples: Ordinary least squares (closed form). Student t p-values from the regularised incomplete beta function...
